candidates: When adding a new demo page under `demos/`, register it with a link in `demos/index.html` so it appears in the demo index.

Do not add individual sub-type exports to `packages/parser/src/index.ts` for every AST node sub-property. Instead, export the `RecursiveAstOmit<T>` utility from the parser package and use it in consuming code (e.g., in diagram `types.ts`) to derive clean, non-`AstNode` types from the top-level exported AST type.

In Langium grammar files, define the `INT` terminal as `/0|[1-9][0-9]*/` to disallow leading zeros (e.g., `00` would otherwise parse as a valid integer, which TypeScript and JavaScript do not accept as a numeric literal).

In Langium diagram grammars where `NEWLINE` tokens are semantically significant, do not use `\s+` as a hidden rule (it would subsume NEWLINE and break rule matching). Require `NEWLINE+` after each block-level rule to prevent multiple blocks from appearing on the same line. The entry rule must also require at least one `NEWLINE` between the diagram keyword and any content so that blocks cannot appear on the same line as the keyword.

Prefix all diagram-specific rule names in Langium `.langium` files with the diagram identifier (e.g., `PacketBlock` not `Block`) to prevent naming collisions across diagram grammars and with Langium built-in AST node types.
Use two-space indentation throughout `.langium` grammar files, consistent with the project's Langium formatting convention.

In a diagram's `styles.ts`: (a) type the exported styles function as `DiagramStylesProvider` (from `../../diagram-api/types.js`); (b) define a named default style-options constant (e.g., `defaultPacketStyleOptions`); and (c) merge caller-supplied options with that constant using `cleanAndMerge` rather than hard-coding defaults inline.

When registering a new diagram's config entry in `defaultConfig.ts`, explicitly set `useMaxWidth: true` to remain consistent with all other diagrams (only `gitGraph` intentionally deviates from this default).

Place all AST-to-DB population logic (walking the parsed AST and calling DB mutation methods) in the diagram's `parser.ts`, not in `db.ts`. The `db.ts` module should expose only mutation and query methods; the parser drives state population.
Export the renderer object in a diagram's `renderer.ts` typed as `DiagramRenderer` (from `../../diagram-api/types.js`), not as a plain object literal.

When defining a diagram-specific `*DB` interface that extends `DiagramDBBase`, explicitly re-declare any optional `DiagramDB` fields the diagram provides (e.g., `getDiagramTitle`, `setAccTitle`, `getAccDescription`) to make them required rather than relying on the inherited optional signature.

In `config.schema.yaml`, always include an explicit `type` field for every property definition; do not rely on type inference from the `default` value. For count, size, or dimension properties that must be non-negative integers, use `type: integer` together with a `minimum` constraint.

Place all type and interface definitions for a diagram module—data structures, domain types, and style option interfaces—in the diagram's `types.ts` file. Do not define them inline in `db.ts` or `styles.ts`.

In a diagram's `db.ts`, use `cleanAndMerge` to combine the default config with the user-provided config rather than using plain object spread (e.g., `cleanAndMerge({ ...DEFAULT_PACKET_CONFIG, ...commonGetConfig().packet })`).
Use strict equality operators (`===` / `!==`) instead of loose equality (`==` / `!=`) throughout TypeScript source files.

Extract unexplained numeric literals (magic numbers) in parser and renderer logic into named constants with descriptive names (e.g., `const MAX_PACKET_SIZE = 10_000`) rather than embedding them inline.
In diagram renderers, call `configureSvgSize(svg, height, width, config.useMaxWidth)` before setting the SVG `viewbox` attribute, following the established pattern in `pieRenderer.ts`.

Diagram unit test files (`*.spec.ts`) must include explicit test cases for diagram metadata fields (`getDiagramTitle`, `getAccTitle`, `getAccDescription`); do not delegate metadata coverage solely to Cypress e2e tests.
